results.title: The role of receptive arts and culture to improve anxiety, depression and psycho
results.reason: This realist review examines how receptive arts and cultural engagement affects anxiety, depression, and psychological distress in young people, with clear clinical relevance for mental health interventions and therapeutic approaches.
results.authors: Daniel Hayes; Joely Wright; Louise Chandler; Kayleigh Albaya de Gago; Summi Ng; Joe Langley; Daisy Fancourt; Kamaldeep Bhui; Roisin Mooney; Rebecca Sheriff

results.title: EcoTherapistVR: Design and Proof-of-Concept Implementation of a Decentralized Bl
results.reason: This paper focuses on technology development (blockchain-based VR platform) rather than clinical psychology practice. While it mentions nature therapy benefits, the core contribution is technical implementation of a digital platform without clinical validation, psychological measures, or direct therapeutic applications relevant to practicing clinicians.

results.title: Protocol for a systematic review of Accelerated Resolution Therapy (ART®) for th
results.reason: Systematic review protocol examining a specific trauma-focused therapy (ART®) for PTSD in adults, which has direct clinical relevance for trauma treatment practitioners
results.authors: David Paul Storey; Emily Claire Shaw Marriott; Josh Rash

results.title: Personalized Prediction of Momentary Affect with Passive Smartphone Sensing Data
results.reason: The paper evaluates machine learning approaches for predicting momentary affect, stress, and energy using passive smartphone sensing data in a clinically diverse sample, with direct implications for digital mental health monitoring and clinical practice.
results.authors: Grant Alexander King; Colin Vize; Adriene Beltz; Aidan G.C. Wright

results.title: Cognitive functioning and Anxiety/Depression: Accounting for Genetic Confounding
results.reason: This paper directly examines cognitive functioning in relation to depression and anxiety, which has clear clinical implications for assessment and intervention. The study addresses a key question in clinical psychology about whether cognitive deficits represent causal risk factors or shared etiological influences with mood/anxiety disorders.
results.authors: Susan Robinson; Jiayao Xu; Hannah Jones; Ian Penton-Voak; Laura D. Howe
